paper.title: Neural Wave Functions for High-Pressure Atomic Hydrogen
paper.authors: David Linteau, Saverio Moroni, Giuseppe Carleo, Markus Holzmann

results.system_description: Static hydrogen: 16 protons pinned to a BCC lattice at r_s = 1.31, cubic cell of 2x2x2 conventional cells, PBC (Gamma), 8 up and 8 down electrons, Ewald sums including the proton-proton term
results.variant: MPNN backflow with Gaussian Bloch orbitals (static protons)
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the optimized message-passing backflow wave function for the electrons in the field of static protons (Born-Oppenheimer), Table I; the DMC and RMC rows of the table are other methods.
results.notes: Energy per atom, Hartree, as printed in v3. Cell volume 4 pi N r_s^3 / 3 (Method); protons on a perfect BCC lattice; the proton coordinates are not printed and follow from the BCC lattice in the cubic cell. Electron spin sector not stated; the reference calculations it is compared with are unpolarized.

results.system_description: Dynamic hydrogen: 16 electrons and 16 quantum protons at r_s = 1.31, cubic cell of 2x2x2 conventional cells, PBC (Gamma), nuclear wave function localized around BCC sites, no proton exchange
results.variant: MPNN backflow with Gaussian Bloch orbitals and a proton MPNN (quantum protons)
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the optimized electron-proton wave function, with electrons and protons both sampled (beyond Born-Oppenheimer), Table II; the SJ-LDA and BF-PW rows are other methods.
results.notes: Energy per atom, Hartree. Hamiltonian Eq. (1): kinetic energy of electrons and protons and all Coulomb terms by Ewald summation; the nuclear factor is Gaussians localized around BCC lattice sites (Table II caption) and proton statistics are neglected. The proton mass is not printed (m_p/m_e = 1836 to the precision that matters here).
